solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Having had small refill, cork

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
to refill a glass or tank is to top it up

explanation.surface: A bottle has been topped up with a little more and then corked.
explanation.definitionFit: To cork a bottle is to plug or seal its neck, which is a synonym of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Covered up in stiff paper, it's strong

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole assembled piece is read from the bottom, so it is turned round
the word it's sits inside the stiff paper

parts.note: card is stiff paper
taken as its letters, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Something wrapped in card is said to be robust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covered up' looks like concealment, but 'up' reverses the whole of CITSARD, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are strong, severe or extreme ones, a looser synonym.

clue.text: No sign of — absent from event

parts.note: someone absent from a place is not at it
a race is a sporting event

explanation.surface: A competitor fails to show up at a meeting, leaving no sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means without any trace or indication, so it answers to having no sign of something.

clue.text: Timeless secrets unfolded in break

indicators.note: the remaining letters are opened out and laid again in a new order
read as time-less: the letter standing for time is removed from the next word

explanation.surface: Eternal mysteries are revealed during an interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' takes T (time) out of SECRETS, leaving SECRES, and 'unfolded' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is a break or pause, as in Parliament's holidays or a school playtime.

clue.text: Can shoot, though second-rate

parts.note: a tin is a can
to pot is to shoot, as at game

explanation.surface: Someone can fire a gun, though not very well.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinpot is a dismissive adjective for something inferior, petty or of poor quality.

clue.text: Vandalised letter boxes round surrounding area and stand

indicators.note: a damaged or wrecked word has its letters jumbled
the letter word takes the round piece in among its own letters before the jumble
the letter word also gathers the area piece in, so all go into one pool

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Vandals damage letter boxes on a round, and the local area has to put up with it.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled LETTER takes O and A into separate gaps, T(O)LER(A)TE; 'boxes' and 'surrounding' each signal one of those insertions.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to put up with or bear it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Marks 'Property of Hell?'

definitions.meaning: small cuts or notches made on a surface
Old Nick is a nickname for the Devil, so what belongs to him is his, with an apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone tags items as belonging to the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Small cuts are nicks, and the possessive of the Devil's nickname gives the same letters.

clue.text: Either retiring or friendly and sociable

definitions.meaning: leaving a post, as an official stepping down at term's end

explanation.surface: A person is described as either shy or gregarious, apparently opposites.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads retiring as shy, the opposite of sociable; here it means leaving office.
explanation.definitionFit: A departing chairman is the leaving one, and an extrovert is also described by the same adjective.

clue.text: Deliver pie

definitions.meaning: to hand something over to someone
a pastry folded over a filling, such as apple

explanation.definitionFit: Handing something over is a phrasal-verb sense, and a folded pastry with fruit inside is the baker's noun.

clue.text: Attending in lieu to appease

indicators.note: the attending word goes inside the lieu word

parts.note: lieu means place, as in in lieu of
to be at an event is to attend it

explanation.surface: Turning up instead of someone else in order to keep the peace.
explanation.definitionFit: To appease someone is to pacify or mollify them, a straight synonym.

clue.text: On to B for 'bucatini'?

parts.note: to go on beyond something is to go past it
the letter that leads to B in the alphabet is A

explanation.surface: A note on moving from one item to the next, the B-word being bucatini.
explanation.walkthrough: Read together, moving on to B means you are past A.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucatini is a thick spaghetti-like tube, an example of the Italian food, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Member of team in Bermudas and T-shirt?

parts.note: Bermudas are knee-length shorts
a T-shirt is an example of a top, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A player on a team is dressed in casual summer clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball, the fielder between second and third base is a member of the fielding side.

clue.text: Bite top off — or cut

indicators.note: in a down clue the top letter is the first, and it is taken away

parts.note: to chew is to bite repeatedly

explanation.surface: Instructions to bite the end off something or slice it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top off' removes C, the first letter of CHEW in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To hew is to cut or chop, typically with an axe.

clue.text: Writing round border in yellow

indicators.note: the writing word goes around the border word

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Text runs around a decorative edge printed in yellow ink.
explanation.definitionFit: The pale yellow colour is named after the spring flower of that shade.

clue.text: Delightful thank you card

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
a king is a playing card

explanation.surface: A lovely thank-you card arrives in the post.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking is a dated adjective for charming or attractive, a synonym.

clue.text: Derogatory remark about waist that's going too far

definitions.meaning: a slighting comment that someone's middle is rather broad

explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means unreasonable or excessive, and literally would describe a somewhat broad waistline.

clue.text: Showing effects of years in prison?

definitions.text: Showing effects of years in prison?

parts.words: Showing effects of years in prison?
parts.note: doing time in jail is serving time, so someone worn by that time inside has a weathered look

explanation.walkthrough: Doing time means serving a prison sentence, so the clue jokes about being worn down by time inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aged and battered by long use is weathered by the years, a synonym of the adjective.

clue.text: Character said what tells character when to speak

definitions.text: what tells character when to speak

indicators.note: the letter is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Q is a letter, i.e. a character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An actor playing a part hears a line that signals when to come in.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'character' is a letter of the alphabet; the second is a role in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre, the signal for an actor's entrance or line is the prompt word, a stage term.

clue.text: Not having been polished by daily?

definitions.text: Not having been polished by daily?

parts.words: Not having been polished by daily?
parts.note: a daily is both a cleaning woman and a daily newspaper, whose staff polish copy before print

explanation.walkthrough: A daily is British slang for a cleaner, so polish looks like housework; read as a newspaper, polishing is editing.
explanation.definitionFit: Text that has not been revised or corrected is raw, which is what the adjective means.

clue.text: Network group of us bought, ought to junk

parts.note: a group that includes us is we

indicators.note: to junk something is to throw it away, so these letters are removed from the word before

parts.note: taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: A group of us made a purchase that we really ought to throw away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to junk' removes OUGHT from BOUGHT, leaving B.
explanation.definitionFit: A web is a network or interconnected mesh, as of threads or contacts.

clue.text: So grasp to turn off

parts.note: sic is Latin for so or thus
ken is understanding or grasp, as in beyond one's ken

explanation.surface: Instructions to grip something and twist it off.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn someone off is to disgust or repel them, a synonym in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Female that, boarding bus, may get items from garden centre

definitions.meaning: the pronoun used for a woman

definitions.text: that, boarding bus, may get items from garden centre
definitions.meaning: put inside the word bus, the pronoun produces shrubs bought at a garden centre

explanation.surface: A woman gets on a bus to go shopping for plants.
explanation.walkthrough: Placing the pronoun inside BUS makes BUSHES, the garden-centre items.
explanation.definitionFit: The third-person pronoun for a woman stands for any female person.

clue.text: This is fabricated — everything in it is somewhat implausible

indicators.note: the everything word goes into the rebuilt word
something fabricated is made up, so the word before is rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone declares a story made up, the whole of it hard to believe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is fabricated' gives TISH, and 'in it' houses everything there; 'This' reads as a pronoun but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is one hard to believe, and the suffix softens it to rather incredible.

clue.text: Hitch old airline's admitted to in warm weather

indicators.note: the airline is let into the hitch word

parts.note: to hitch is to pull or haul up, as a heave does
TWA was Trans World Airlines, a defunct American carrier

explanation.surface: A problem with a defunct airline has been owned up to amid hot weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hitch' looks like a snag but here means a pull or haul.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell of unusually hot weather is the meteorological term, so warm weather is a mild description.

clue.text: Technically, more than half rioting could be racial

indicators.note: the chosen letters run riot into a new order
only the opening six of the word's eleven letters are kept, more than half of it

explanation.surface: Strictly speaking, most of the unrest might be about race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than half' keeps TECHNI, dropping the last five letters of Technically, and 'rioting' rearranges it; 'could be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnic relates to a people's shared race or culture, a near synonym.

clue.text: Feel destiny has it in store for family heir?

indicators.note: the phrase holds the letters inside it, like goods kept in a store

explanation.surface: A sense that fate has something planned for the family's successor.
explanation.definitionFit: The firstborn child is typically the one who inherits, hence heir with a question mark as an example.

clue.text: Tennis watched on TV in bedroom?

definitions.meaning: part of a tennis match, the one after the first
an extra television in the bedroom is a household's spare receiver

explanation.surface: Someone watches the tennis on the bedroom television.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis match divides into sets, and a spare television counts as another receiver in the house.

clue.text: Award zero mark

parts.note: O looks like zero
a scar is a mark left on the skin

explanation.surface: A judge awards a score of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Award statuette is a famous film prize.

clue.text: Said cargo compartment is no longer watertight

indicators.note: the word is spoken, sounding like the answer

parts.note: a ship's hold is where cargo is stowed

explanation.surface: A ship's cargo space is reported to be leaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A hull with a hole punched in it lets water in, so it is no longer sealed.

clue.text: Don't allow when junior gets to bed on time

parts.note: a junior is a boy
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A parent refuses permission when a child is put to bed on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: To boycott is to refuse to support or take part, a near synonym of shunning.

clue.text: Gives non-fishing actor angling role — with these results?

definitions.text: Gives non-fishing actor angling role — with these results?

parts.words: Gives non-fishing actor angling role — with these results?
parts.note: a director who hires a wrong actor gets wrong casting, and an angler who has never fished throws the line badly

explanation.walkthrough: The verb does both jobs: a director gives a role badly, and the actor's bad throws of the line are the results.
explanation.definitionFit: Casting an actor wrongly is the verb's sense, and bungled throws of a fishing line are the noun's.

clue.text: Caught sand storms circling again?

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes around the again word
storms means the word is whipped up into a new order

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: Sandstorms whirl around once more and trap someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sand storms' reads as one word, sandstorms, but 'storms' is the signal, giving SNAD, which 'circling' wraps round the prefix for again.
explanation.definitionFit: To be snared is to be trapped or captured, a synonym of caught.
